generation_notes: Revised to exactly 18 structurally valid MODBUS/TCP seed sequences with corrected MBAP length fields, removed unsupported evidence references, reduced redundant 0x11 duplication, and added stronger coverage for simple read functions, diagnostics baseline, mask write, and FIFO access. All seeds preserve MBAP framing with protocol_id=0x0000 and length equal to unit_id plus PDU bytes per the documented MBAP header. Issue-guided seeds keep only safer structural analogues grounded in the supplied issue summaries, especially around repeated write behavior and conservative 0x17 variants, while avoiding exact historical crash payloads and repairing field relations such as byte counts and quantities.

request body is starting address followed by quantity

sequences.title: Stateful setup for Read/Write Multiple Registers

sequences.expected_behavior: Server should accept the setup write and then parse the 0x17 request that reads one register from 0x0010 and writes one register to 0x0020.
constraints_preserved: both messages have complete MBAP headers
first length is 0006 for unit_id plus 5-byte 0x06 PDU
second length is 000d for unit_id plus 12-byte 0x17 PDU

sequences.title: Boundary-adjacent Read File Record

sequences.title: Issue-guided repeated valid write analogue

global_feedback: The library has strong operation diversity and generally uses complete MBAP framing with sensible big-endian field encodings.
Several seeds are practically useful as initial corpus material because they are canonical valid requests or conservative stateful sequences likely to reach normal parser paths.

A small but important set of framing and evidence-quality issues lowers confidence: multiple seeds state incorrect MBAP length values in their preserved-constraints text, one seed has an actual on-wire MBAP length mismatch, and one issue-guided seed cites an unrelated issue.
The best seeds are the canonical 0x03 read, the 0x17 stateful sequence, the 0x2B/0x0E nested request, the fixed-size 0x05 and 0x06 writes, and the well-formed 0x10 write.

The weakest area is over-allocation of slots to diagnostics and lightweight simple reads while some more structurally rich functions from the coverage summary are absent or not aligned to the requested plans.

Issue enhancement is only partially convincing: the repeated-write analogue is a reasonable safe structural motif, and the quantity-7 read is acceptable, but some plan-to-seed mappings drift and the historical issue linkage is not always well grounded.
For a desired final selected seed count of 12, this library should be trimmed to the strongest 12 and revised to fix the framing mismatch and misleading annotations before acceptance.

Template: MBAP Header
- Field: transaction_id
  Description: Protocol field 'transaction_id'. Layer: mbap. Role: control. Type: uint16. Range: [0, 65535]. Inferred-from: wire. Binding-strength: explicit_check. Evidence-type: compare.
  Length: 16 bits
  Protocol constraints: must match request transaction_id echoed in response
  Implementation constraints: checked byte-by-byte at offsets 0 and 1, used for request/response pairing
- Field: protocol_id
  Description: Protocol field 'protocol_id'. Layer: mbap. Role: meta. Type: uint16. Constraints: value must be 0 (0x0000). Range: [0, 0]. Inferred-from: wire. Binding-strength: explicit_check. Evidence-type: compare.
  Length: 16 bits
  Protocol constraints: protocol_id == 0
  Implementation constraints: must be 0x0000 for Modbus
- Field: length
  Description: Protocol field 'length'. Layer: mbap. Role: length. Type: uint16. Constraints: must equal total frame size minus 6 octets, sent big-endian. Range: [1, 253]. Inferred-from: wire. Binding-strength: direct_byte_parse. Evidence-type: offset.
  Length: 16 bits
  Implementation constraints: covers Unit-ID + PDU only
- Field: unit_id
  Description: Protocol field 'unit_id'. Layer: mbap. Role: address. Type: uint8. Constraints: range 0-255. Range: [0, 255]. Inferred-from: wire. Binding-strength: direct_byte_parse. Evidence-type: offset.

Issue: 743
Summary: In libmodbus 3.1.10, the modbus_write_bits function reportedly has a heap-buffer-overflow caused by an out-of-bounds read of the input buffer when specially crafted input makes the nb (number of bits) parameter read past available data. The sample input provided is <00><01><02><00><80><04><01><01><2A>. The report says this produces undefined behavior and crashes, with ASan indicating a heap-buffer-overflow; the mention of other unintended behaviors is speculative.
Reproduce: Reported environment: libmodbus 3.1.10 on Linux/Ubuntu 20.04 amd64. No specific example program, build flags, or command line is given, but the report says libmodbus debug mode was enabled and refers to ASan reports. To reproduce as documented: 1) Run a libmodbus instance with debug output enabled so it accepts a client connection and waits for an indication. 2) Provide the sample input <00><01><02><00><80><04><01><01><2A>. 3) Observe the debug output shown in the report: "Client connection accepted from 127.0.0.1.", "Waiting for an indication...", "ERROR Connection timed out: select", the sample input, and "Quit the loop: Connection timed out". Expected result: ASan reports a heap-buffer-overflow in modbus_write_bits due to an out-of-bounds read of the input buffer, and the function exhibits undefined behavior/crashes.

Issue: 614
Summary: The report describes a heap-based buffer overflow in libmodbus triggered by a crafted request sent to the test server. The issue title names modbus_reply, while the description names _modbus_receive_msg; the provided AddressSanitizer trace shows the fault in modbus_reply at src/modbus.c:980:46. When tests/unit-test-server processes the supplied byte sequence, the observed result is a server abort: first with "double free or corruption (!prev)", and in the ASan run with a SEGV caused by a WRITE memory access in modbus_reply.
Reproduce: Use the libmodbus test server program tests/unit-test-server.c. Run ./unit-test-server (the report also shows ./tests/unit-test-server). From a client, connect to the server and send the exact byte sequence <03><DD><00><00><00><0D><FF><17><01><62><00><01><00><84><00><01><02><D7><11>. In the documented debug-enabled run, the server logs that the client connection from 127.0.0.1 is accepted, prints the received request, emits [03][DD][00][00][00][05][FF][17][02][00][00], then logs "ERROR Connection reset by peer: read", "Quit the loop: Connection reset by peer", and aborts with "double free or corruption (!prev)". In an AddressSanitizer build, sending the same input causes a SEGV on a WRITE access in modbus_reply at src/modbus.c:980:46, followed by process abort.

Issue: 738
Summary: In libmodbus-3.1.10, an intermittent crash is reported in `read_registers()` in `modbus.c` at line 1313, reached from `modbus_read_input_registers(ctx, 0, 7, reg)`. The failing statement is the loop that stores response data into `dest[i]`; the provided backtrace shows `dest=0x1` and inaccessible at that point. The report does not identify the root cause or a specific missing validation, although the reporter states the original `reg` array address looked valid in gdb. The documented trigger is reading 7 input registers starting at address 0 from the device, and the demonstrated impact is an intermittent process crash.
Reproduce: Use libmodbus-3.1.10 and a program like the reporter's `pollExternalDevice.cpp`, where `main()` calls `modbus_read_input_registers(ctx, 0, 7, reg)` (reported at line 366) to read 7 input registers starting at address 0 from the device. Repeat the read operation; the report says it is "not reproduceble everytime" and "crashing sometimes." When it fails, inspect under gdb/debug mode: the backtrace shows frame `#0 read_registers` at `modbus.c:1313` on the `dest[i] = ...` assignment, with `dest=0x1`, and frame `#1 main()` at `pollExternalDevice.cpp:366`. No standalone PoC or exact command sequence is provided.

Issue: 764
Summary: In libmodbus v3.1.6, an invalid pointer dereference is reported in modbus.c. The issue can be triggered by sending a specific packet to the unit-test-server program. The observed result is a crash, shown in the report as an AddressSanitizer SEGV. The report further states that the issue appears to be caused by the backend_type pointer not being properly initialized, but that cause is presented as apparent/speculative rather than demonstrated.
Reproduce: 1. Use libmodbus v3.1.6 and run the unit-test-server target.
2. Send the documented PoC packet to the server: 00000000000CFF1701600002006B0001021234
3. The reported result is a crash instead of normal handling; the document shows an AddressSanitizer diagnostic beginning with: "ERROR: AddressSanitizer: SEGV on unknown address 0x605ffffffe96".

global_feedback: Most seeds use complete MBAP framing with correct protocol_id and generally correct length fields, which is the strongest aspect of the library.
The corpus has good entry-point diversity across read, write, file-record, encapsulated transport, and diagnostics operations.

The requested selected seed count is 12, but the candidate library contains 18 seeds and includes clear redundancy, especially among the three Report Server ID analogues and the three diagnostics counter variants.

Several seeds rely on operation layouts that are only partially supported by the provided sources; those should be treated more cautiously than the canonical 0x03, 0x04, 0x05, 0x06, 0x08, 0x10, and 0x11 requests.
There are protocol-validity issues in at least three seeds due to incorrect MBAP length values: modbustcp-seed-003, modbustcp-seed-014, and modbustcp-seed-015.

Issue-guided enhancement is mixed: the seeds avoid direct crash-payload replay, which is good, but several issue analogues are only loosely connected to the cited issue structure and therefore add limited value.
Deterministic validator evidence-id removals are not themselves fatal, but they correlate with weaker grounding for several issue-guided and function-coverage seeds.
The best retained set should prioritize canonical-valid requests plus the stateful 0x17 sequence, then trim duplicates and seeds with framing errors.

coverage_gaps: No canonical coverage for 0x01 Read Coils or 0x02 Read Discrete Inputs, both useful simple parser entry points.

global_feedback: The library has strong operation diversity and generally uses complete MBAP framing with sensible big-endian field encodings.
Several seeds are practically useful as initial corpus material because they are canonical valid requests or conservative stateful sequences likely to reach normal parser paths.

A small but important set of framing and evidence-quality issues lowers confidence: multiple seeds state incorrect MBAP length values in their preserved-constraints text, one seed has an actual on-wire MBAP length mismatch, and one issue-guided seed cites an unrelated issue.
The best seeds are the canonical 0x03 read, the 0x17 stateful sequence, the 0x2B/0x0E nested request, the fixed-size 0x05 and 0x06 writes, and the well-formed 0x10 write.

The weakest area is over-allocation of slots to diagnostics and lightweight simple reads while some more structurally rich functions from the coverage summary are absent or not aligned to the requested plans.

Issue enhancement is only partially convincing: the repeated-write analogue is a reasonable safe structural motif, and the quantity-7 read is acceptable, but some plan-to-seed mappings drift and the historical issue linkage is not always well grounded.
For a desired final selected seed count of 12, this library should be trimmed to the strongest 12 and revised to fix the framing mismatch and misleading annotations before acceptance.
